subject: Exploring Aurora white-label: embedding Redwood runtime into Aurora Console
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.b@aurorasystems.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Menon <p.menon@aurorasystems.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interest in embedding Redwood runtime into Aurora Console

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for taking this. Aurora is evaluating a tighter embed of an LLM runtime into our customer admin console (white-label experience). We’d like the runtime to be indistinguishable to our customers (Aurora branding only), and we need tight cost predictability for enterprise customers.

Attached is a brief doc with our integration requirements (high level). Key asks upfront:
- Can Redwood support a branded embed (no Redwood logos in product UI)?
- Options for hosted vs on-prem/private deployment for enterprise buyers
- Expected latency for 512 token generation at ~25–40 rps per org
- Commercial models for OEM / revenue share vs per-call billing

Would love to hop on a call this week and share more. Priya is our product lead and will coordinate the POC scope.

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Head of Integrations, Aurora Systems
Attachments: Aurora_Integ_Requirements.pdf (pdf, 132KB)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Menon <p.menon@aurorasystems.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in embedding Redwood runtime into Aurora Console

Hi Evan —

Great to meet you (virtually). I’ve looped in Karthik (commercial lead) and Monica (partner PM). Happy to run through the attachment and set a technical + commercial kickoff. Two quick asks so we can come prepared:

1) Do you expect Aurora to resell the runtime as part of your SaaS (single invoice to end customers) or act as a pass-through where Aurora bills separately?
2) Are we looking for a fully skin-able front-end (JS/CSS) or only backend branding (responses stamped as Aurora)?
3) Any data residency or audit requirements for the POC (EU customers in-scope?)
4) Target POC metrics (qps, latency p95, concurrency) and target timeline (4–8 weeks typical)

I’ll draft a proposed POC scope and a lightweight OEM SLA for discussion. Are you available Fri 4/16 10:00–11:00 PT?

—Stephanie
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0184

Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers:
- Commercial: Aurora prefers to bundle the runtime into our SaaS and issue a single invoice to customers (we’ll need a white-label reseller arrangement).
- Branding: We want a full skin — Aurora UI controls, no Redwood mark in the UX. Backend call traces can contain "powered-by" metadata for troubleshooting (visible to our admins only).
- Residency: POC should cover US initially, but our enterprise pipeline includes EU customers in Q3; we’ll need data residency options for GA.
- Performance: For the POC target, ~30 rps at 512-token avg generation with p95 latency < 350ms for simple prompts.
- Timeline: Hoping for a 6-week POC, show an integration in customer-facing UI by week 4.

Priya will be on the call Fri. Attached: clarifying notes to the requirements.

Best,
Evan
Attachments: Aurora_Integ_Requirements.pdf (updated)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Aurora white-label embed — initial commercial/tech framing

Folks —

Aurora wants a full skinning experience + reseller billing. POC targets ~30 rps, p95 <350ms, US-first with EU on roadmap. I drafted a lightweight OEM SLA and included a few commercial options below. Please review and flag any hard no's.

Commercial options (summary):
- Hosted OEM (Redwood-hosted, white-label via iframe/SDK): per-token billing + reseller margin; lower operational lift; faster POC
- Dedicated Reserved (Dedicated GPU pool for Aurora): monthly commit for reserved capacity, predictable unit economics, supports stricter audit/SLA
- Private (VPC or on-premise): enterprise-only; highest margin; long lead time and additional compliance work

Suggested POC pricing (internal): 50% off list for 6-week POC, capped monthly token spend $12k. If we go dedicated for GA, propose a 12-month commit with tiered discounts and a rev-share option for co-sold accounts.

Security/compliance asks to prepare: SOC 2 evidence, data retention controls, ingress/egress encryption, customer audit logs. I attached the Draft_OEM_SLA.docx — please add notes inline.

—Steph
Attachments: Draft_OEM_SLA.docx

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurora white-label embed — initial commercial/tech framing

Agree with Steph's framing. A few concrete points:

- Recommend starting with Hosted OEM for POC (fastest path). We can lift to Dedicated Reserved if Aurora requires predictable latency/SLA for early enterprise pilots.
- POC discount: 50% off reasonable. Cap spend like you suggested.
- Rev-share: for co-sell accounts we can offer 10–20% on net revenue for 12 months, then revisit.
- SLA: p99 target for dedicated is 1s; hosted OEM we offer best-effort with a 99.5% availability SLO. We can include automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model if we have capacity issues.
- Security: link to checklist: https://internal.redwood/sales/security-checklist (use when responding to Aurora)
- HubSpot: I created a deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/DEAL-AUR-2027-023

If Monica can own partner ops and run the onboarding checklist, I’ll draft the commercial term sheet (paper) for the reseller model.

—Karthik
